topics.title: Big-O Cheat Sheet
topics.description: Complexity of the data structures that cover almost every live-coding round, plus how to read the target complexity straight off the input constraints.
topics.sorting: Arrays.sort is O(n log n): dual-pivot quicksort for primitives, TimSort for objects (stable).
reading_the_constraints: n up to 10^5 to 10^6: you need O(n) or O(n log n).
n up to about 1000: O(n^2) is fine.
n up to about 20: exponential or bitmask solutions are acceptable.

topics.title: Hashing & Counting
topics.description: Trade memory for a lookup. The first thing to try when a brute force does repeated searching.
topics.say_out_loud: Can I trade memory for a lookup?

topics.title: Two Pointers
topics.description: Walk two indices over sorted data, or inward from both ends, to drop a nested loop.
use_for: Pair sum in a sorted array

topics.title: Sliding Window
topics.description: Grow the window on the right, shrink from the left while it violates the invariant. For subarray and substring problems with a property.
use_for: Maximum sum of a window of size k

topics.title: Stack
topics.description: Matching, nearest-greater and undo problems. A monotonic stack answers next-greater questions in one pass.

topics.title: Binary Search
topics.description: Classic search on sorted data, and the harder variant: binary search the answer space for the minimum value that satisfies a condition.
use_for: Find a target in a sorted array
Search in a rotated sorted array
Minimum capacity or speed satisfying a condition (Koko eating bananas, ship packages in D days)

topics.title: BFS & DFS
topics.description: Breadth-first for shortest path and level order; depth-first for trees, islands and backtracking. Backtracking is choose, recurse, un-choose.
use_for: BFS: tree level order, rotten oranges, word ladder, shortest steps in a grid
DFS: number of islands, maximum tree depth, path sum

templates.title: BFS by levels on a grid
Backtracking (permutations)

topics.title: Heap & Top-K
topics.description: Keep a heap of size K instead of sorting everything. Also the tool for K-way merges.
use_for: K largest or Kth largest element
K closest points to the origin
Meeting rooms: min heap of end times

topics.title: Prefix Sums & Intervals
topics.description: Two small patterns that show up constantly and take one line of setup each.

patterns.description: Precompute running totals so any range sum is O(1). Combine with a HashMap of seen prefixes for subarray sum equals K.
Sort by start, then merge overlapping intervals in one sweep. Meeting rooms uses a min heap of end times to count concurrent intervals.

topics.title: Dynamic Programming
topics.description: Recognize it, do not fear it. Framework: state, recurrence, base case, iteration order. Say the four out loud; a one-dimensional table usually suffices in an interview.

topics.title: Graphs & Topo Sort
topics.description: Model the input as an adjacency list first, then pick the traversal. BFS with in-degrees (Kahn's algorithm) is the easiest topological sort to code live.
use_for: Any problem phrased as nodes and prerequisites

topics.title: Java Live-Coding Tips
topics.description: Small choices that make the code read as idiomatic Java under time pressure.
tips: Use Deque (ArrayDeque) for stacks and queues, not Stack or LinkedList.
Use StringBuilder inside loops; s.toCharArray() for character iteration.
Map.merge and computeIfAbsent shorten counting code: map.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(v);
Streams are fine for one-liners, but write explicit loops when the interviewer wants to see complexity thinking.
Guard integer overflow: use long for sums and products, and lo + (hi - lo) / 2 for the midpoint.

topics.title: Interview Loop & Plan
topics.description: The spoken routine to run on every problem, plus a four-week practice schedule.
steps: Restate the problem and clarify constraints: sizes, duplicates, negatives, empty input.
Walk one happy path and one edge case by hand.
State the brute force out loud, name its complexity, then improve it (O(n^2) with nested loops; a HashMap gets us to O(n)).
Code while narrating. Small helper methods keep it clean.
Trace the example; check edges: empty, single element, all elements equal.
State the final time and space complexity unprompted.
